subject: Re: Dedicated migration — slipstream autoscale and overflow contingency for Zephyryn
messages:
From: Tess Shelby <tess.shelby@zephyryn.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@zephyryn.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated migration — capacity forecast and contingency ask

Marissa / Karthik,

Thanks again for walking us through the Dedicated offering last week. Zephyryn is planning a phased migration from hosted in Jan–Mar and we want to lock down committed slab sizing and a fall-back plan for unpredictable spikes during product launches.

Quick context: our current peak workload generates ~220k tokens/min across a mix of short (<256) and a few long (>2k) chat sessions. For the pilot (Q1), we expect a sustained dedicated footprint of ~8x A100-80GB equivalents with short bursts up to the 12–14x range for 30–60 minute windows during major releases. We budgeted some headroom but want an ops-safe policy that won't cause immediate throttle failures for customers.

Two asks for the contract:
- Can we define a slipstream overflow policy that routes overflow to a pre-approved hosted pool rather than immediate eviction?
- Is there a credit model for short bursts beyond committed slabs (similar to burst credits) and what are the SLO implications?

Attaching our demand scenarios and an early SLA doc for your review.

Appreciate a pragmatic plan — Tess

--
Tess Shelby
Head of Infrastructure, Zephyryn AI
ops@zephyryn.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Tess Shelby <tess.shelby@zephyryn.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated migration — capacity forecast and contingency ask

Tess — thanks for the detailed scenarios, that helps a lot. High-level response before Karthik chimes in with numbers: we can provide a two-tier buffer model that minimizes customer-visible throttles during launches while keeping committed pricing predictable. Outline below; I'll loop Ben for pricing/credits.

1) Slipstream overflow routing (recommended)
- When tenant utilization exceeds committed slab by >10% for >45s, requests will be routed to a pre-authorized hosted pool in the nearest region. Routing happens at the request edge and is sticky per-session for the remainder of that burst window (configurable TTL, default 10 min).
- Hosted fallback uses model-variant parity to preserve response characteristics; if exact variant unavailable, we fall back to a closest-compatible quantized variant with clear quality tags in logs.

2) Short-burst crediting
- We support a short-burst credit bank: small bursts (<= 20% over slab, <= 60 min total per 24h) draw credits automatically when available. When exhausted, overflow routing activates. Credits are billed monthly if consumed; unused credits do not roll over by default (can negotiate a rollover clause).

3) Operational SLOs and observability
- We can commit to <2% customer-visible throttles during declared launch windows if slipstream routing + credits are enabled, with a per-route latency uplift budget (token-level metrics in Console).
- We will provide a launch runbook checklist (traffic gating, canary routing percentage, pre-warm cache keys) and a short-run test window to validate the routing before go-live.

Next steps: Karthik will propose the slab sizing and the headroom numbers, and Ben will propose the burst-credit pricing and contract language. If that looks acceptable, we'll draft an addendum to the SLA for injection into your MSA.

Best,
Marissa

--
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Tess Shelby <tess.shelby@zephyryn.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Nov 2026 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated migration — capacity forecast and contingency ask

Tess / team — dug into the demand scenarios you shared and ran a few synthetic sims with our runtime profile. Top-level sizing guidance:

- Pilot slab (Q1): 8x GPU equivalent mapped as 6x A100-80 + 2x A10-80 mix (to balance cost and long-tail memory needs). This matches your sustained baseline with a 15% buffer for steady growth.
- Headroom for frequent short bursts: we recommend configuring ephemeral slab headroom of +25% available as pre-authorized ephemeral slots. These slots are not guaranteed; they will be pre-warmed and billed as burst credit consumption when used.
- High-impact release windows (15–90 min windows): allow ephemeral uplift up to +75% of committed capacity via slipstream routing to hosted pool; internal throttling only if uplifts exceed that for >90 min.

Eviction and fairness policy notes:
- Eviction will be last-in-first-out by session idle score; long-running KV-heavy sessions get a higher retention weight.
- Priority weights can be configured per route/customer; we'll work with Zephyryn to set a default of 'production-critical' and 'api-noninteractive' categories.

Technical checklist for migration (short):
- Pre-warm KV cache with top 50 session prefixes
- Pin model versions across both dedicated and hosted pools (to avoid drift)
- Canary window: 6 hours at 10% traffic, gradually stepped to 30% before full cutover

Marissa — please loop Ben for the pricing/credits and draft SLA language. Tess — happy to jump on a focused ops call to walk the pre-warm steps.

-karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Tess Shelby <tess.shelby@zephyryn.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated migration — capacity forecast and contingency ask

Tess — following Karthik's sizing notes, here is a pricing sketch for the burst-credit model plus extra contract touches we typically include for slipstream routing: 

- Burst credits: priced at a blended per-token uplift rate tied to the committed slab (example: pilot slab 8x, credit unit priced at 1.7x hosted per-token rate). Credits sold in monthly bundles: 100k, 250k, 1M units. Unused credits: configurable rollover (default: no).
- Ephemeral pre-authorized slots: a small monthly reservation fee to keep capacity pre-warmed (covers idle GPU retention + pre-warm cost). Fee scales with max uplift band (we'll propose bands: 25%, 50%, 75%).
- SLA addendum: we add a 'slipstream routing' clause that defines the fallback pool, quality parity expectations, and an incident tagging requirement so that Zephyryn can filter routing-induced variance in their telemetry.

Action items & attachments:
- I'll prepare a short amendment for the MSA (SLA_Draft_v2.pdf) and a credit pricing appendix. Please review and flag any commercial constraints.
- Marissa: please include the canary runbook checklist we discussed in the Drive folder.

If this commercial sketch looks directionally right, I'll convert to redline-ready language and propose band pricing numbers in the next 48 hours.

Thanks — Ben

--
Ben Carter
Head of Customer Pricing, Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
